message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights (Texas) | Notes | |----------|------------------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords must itemize deductions and provide receipts if requested. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition; repair structural defects, plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.
• Must keep common areas clean and free of hazards. | If landlord fails, tenants may withhold rent, repair & deduct, or terminate lease. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot disturb your peaceful use of the property without cause. | Includes unreasonable entry, noise, or harassment. | | **Entry Notice** | • Landlord must give at least 24‑hour written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | Notice must specify purpose and time. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but must comply with lease terms and give proper notice (usually 30 days). | For some cities, there may be local ordinances limiting increases. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing for >1 year.
• Must include rent amount, due date, security deposit, lease term, and rules. | Oral leases are enforceable but harder to prove. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | Federal Fair Housing Act applies statewide. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease termination).
• Eviction must follow court procedures; unlawful detainer actions require filing in county court. | Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If landlord fails to fix major problems, tenant may repair and deduct cost from rent, or pay and get reimbursement. | Must notify landlord first and keep receipts. | | **Right to Access Records** | • Tenant can request copies of lease, inspection reports, and maintenance records. | Landlord must provide within a reasonable timeframe. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Generally allowed unless lease prohibits it; landlord may not unreasonably refuse sublease. | Subtenant must meet same screening criteria. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide hot water, electricity, gas, and water unless otherwise specified. | Some utilities may be tenant responsibility per lease. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Ensure all promises (maintenance, repairs, deposit return) are documented. 2. **Document Issues** – Take photos, keep written communication, and note dates of complaints. 3. **Serve Proper Notices** – Use certified mail or hand delivery with receipt for any formal notices. 4. **Know Local Ordinances** – Some Texas cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protection laws. 5. **Seek Legal Aid** – If disputes arise, consult a local attorney or tenant advocacy group. --- #### Want a Sample Lease? If you’re drafting a lease or need a template tailored to Texas law, let me know the type of lease (e.g., residential, commercial), parties involved, and any special provisions you’d like included. I can generate a draft using the `generate_contract` tool.
